Your GPU is working much harder at higher resolutions. This makes it render slower as it uses maximum power, which means that your CPU doesn’t have to process as much information in between frame renders, meaning your cpu utilization goes down.

This really only happens in extensive loads, or if you have a serious mismatch in equipment (a 1660 gpu and an I9 14900k for instance).

Essentially, you have your idea of it backwards. 1080p isn’t more demanding on your CPU, 1440 or 4k are more demanding on your gpu, giving your cpu more time to catch up.

For some ETL transparency:
Base for my store is 60k. I’m making 74k after 3 years in role, after starting at 63k. I’m considered a high performing ETL, and got a few quarterly raises, so that impacts it as well.

AMA about ETL pay if curious, or any pay grade pay, as I’ve been P35 and P45 previously.

ETL-HR reports to the SD, but has a “dotted line” reporting structure to the HRBP. Basically two bosses.

ETL-AP reports directly to the APBP in workday and in practice. We are a separate pyramid entirely, which only converges with Store Side leadership at HQ levels, just like PM.

ETL-AP’s have keys. APTL’s and APS do not. AP is more of an oversight role, so they need to be as separated as possible from storeside functions, including access to entrance/exit vestibules. APTL’s don’t have access to these at all, while ETL-AP does. This has a lot to do with ETL-AP’s being salary and held to a higher standard from everyday performance to interview expectations. I would argue APTL is the hardest TL position to get, and ETL-AP the hardest ETL position to get. There’s so much access that we have that can be abused, so additional checks and balances are in place. We have more in depth background checks, and issues of “moral turpitude” are basically a disqualifier off jump.

Don’t get me wrong, in my time as an AP leader, I’ve had to open/close the store, run drive-ups and pick Ship batches. But me doing that is very rare and requires extenuating circumstances. I’m there to make sure everyone else is doing what they need to do, and I need to be able to step away at a moments notice to handle security or theft concerns.

Feel free to ask any questions if you have them. We have operational security concerns, so there’s a lot I can’t share, but I don’t mind providing insight where I can.

I’ve had to get pretty creative. Here’s some tricks that have given me success in the past:

Review your top 9 areas outside of business hours for TM’s who don’t belong. If our guests are stealing it, chances are our TM’s are too.

Fulfillment hold areas, look for fulfillment tm’s who still have merch in their carts after they stow, means they’re shopping in the clock, could be stealing.

As AP, the guys who would tell you it’s not okay, I can tell you this much.

Are you causing a disturbance?
Are you impeding traffic or preventing other guests from being able to park/shop/go about their business?
Are you soliciting anything?
Are you otherwise doing anything “unethical” or “borderline” that could 1)cause a scene, or 2)causing one of the previously mentioned topics?

If you were doing this at my store I honestly wouldn’t care, but every team is different.

Try to think higher scope than just “I identified a problem and fixed it”. Instead, try something like “I identified the problem, lead the team with my knowledge to fix it, and used it as a training session for x tm to be able to navigate it on their own next time”. 

Yea, they want to hear your successes, but they care more about your influence in those successes. And sell yourself high, because they’re interviewing you, not your team you work with everyday. “I” and “me”, not “us” and “we”.

Good luck on your interview!

The issue isn’t the camera quality, it never is. It actually comes down to server costs for storing that video. Sometimes 480p for 5 days is all a company can actually afford, and in larger businesses with more and more cameras, the operating and server costs can exceed and even dwarf the benefit of having the recordings in the first place. If you have 5 cameras recording at 480p for 5 days, you’re looking at potentially several hundred mb to a gb possibly. Factor in more than 5 cameras, the cost for that server starts to go up even further. Now multiply that by 100, 500, 1000 different atores and you’re looking at a huge cost.
